# Introduction

[YOUR CONTENT HERE -- 2-3 paragraphs. Open with an
"I didn't really know..." hook about UltiSnips
Python interpolation. Reference the Stack Overflow
question that prompted this post:
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/78636197

Describe the problem: needing a snippet that
generates a variable number of elements (e.g.,
music chord placeholders). Transition to what
this post will cover.]

More formally, this post documents the Vim-plugins layer
(Layer 6) of the Workflow Construct described in
[post 52](/posts/52-workflow-construct/), specifically
UltiSnips with embedded Python for snippets that require
runtime computation. Static snippets, where the expansion is
literal text, are the simple case; dynamic snippets, where
the expansion runs Python at expansion time, are what make
UltiSnips meaningfully different from a paste buffer. This
post is the dynamic-snippet companion to
[post 30](/posts/30-setupRvimtex/), which covers the static
R-plus-LaTeX snippet vocabulary.

# Prerequisites and Setup

[YOUR CONTENT HERE -- 1-2 paragraphs. What readers
need: Vim 8+ compiled with Python3 support,
UltiSnips plugin installed (via vim-plug, Vundle,
or pathogen). Show how to verify Python support.]

```vim
" Check Python support in Vim
:echo has('python3')

" UltiSnips configuration in .vimrc
Plug 'SirVer/ultisnips'
let g:UltiSnipsExpandTrigger = "<tab>"
let g:UltiSnipsJumpForwardTrigger = "<c-j>"
let g:UltiSnipsJumpBackwardTrigger = "<c-k>"
```

[YOUR CONTENT HERE -- 1-2 paragraphs in plain

## The Chord Generator: Solving the Stack Overflow
  Problem

[YOUR CONTENT HERE -- The core section. Show the
original Stack Overflow problem: generating a
variable number of chord placeholders. Present the
Python function from the original post:]

```python
def make_chords(num_reps):
    text = ""
    for i in range(num_reps):
        text += "< > "
    return text
```
